page.layout: One printed page (left). Running head at top, then running text in one column with a centred heading "ARGVMENTA CAPITVM" and "CAP. I", followed by a verse argument of four stanzas with small marginal numerals at the left, and the catchword at the lower right. The right-hand printed page is only partly visible at the scan edge and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: finitionem verae circumcisionis, & exemplar verae iustificationis in Apostolo, usque ad v. 15. Deinde hortatur Philippenses, ut illud suum exemplum imitentur, & ita sint affecti, ut in solo Christo glorientur.

Cap. I v. verso 1. est conclusio superiorum plena affectuum, ut fit in conclusionibus. Reliqui versus usque ad Conclusionem Epistolae, duo potissimum continent, admonitiones, easque duplices, privatas ad quasdam praecipuas foeminas, inter quas discordia aliquid exortum videtur, (usque ad v. 4.) & generales, ad gaudium spirituale, ad [illegible, ~12 letters], ad preces & virtutes alias, usque ad v.10.11. Gratiarum actionem pro liberalitate Philippensium, usque ad v. 21. ubi est Epistola huius.
Conclusio, in qua petit alios suis verbis salutari: v. 21. salutat eos verbis aliorum: (v.22.) & tandem usitato voto concludit: v. ultimo.
main_text.head: ARGVMENTA CAPITVM
CAP. I
main_text.p: Audeo quod sancti teneatis dogmata Christi, Nec vos, quae patior, damna movere queant. Plus etiam fidei fructus incommoda portant, Sed sanctam referat vita pudica fidem.
2Concordes animi celsos compescite fastus, Hoc etenim Christi vos pia vita docet. Qui quondam vilis, summo nunc fulget honore: Doctores verbi vos coluisse decet.
3Doctores falsos vigilanti mente cavete, Qui cum lege fidem composuisse solent.

page.notes: The first word of the page is a fragment; its first letter is partly hidden by a printer's mark. The Greek words in the line beginning "ad" are too faint to read and are marked illegible. Section numbers and marginal numerals 2 and 3 are set in the left margin beside the verse. The right page is cut off at the scan edge and is not transcribed. The initial G of the verse argument is a large letter joined to "Audeo".
